decks.domain: Driving privilege: points, suspensions and restoration

cards.front: What puts driver license points on your North Carolina driving record?
cards.back: Being convicted of certain motor vehicle violations in North Carolina puts driver license points on your driving record.

cards.front: At what point total may DMV send you to a driver improvement clinic?
cards.back: Once you reach seven points, DMV may send you to a driver improvement clinic, and the clinic costs eighty-three point five zero dollars.

cards.front: How many points does satisfactorily finishing the driver improvement clinic remove?
cards.back: Finishing the driver improvement clinic satisfactorily takes three points off your record.

cards.front: How many points within three years can get your license suspended?
cards.back: Collecting twelve points within three years can get your license suspended.

cards.front: After reinstatement, how many points within three years can bring a second suspension?
cards.back: After your license is reinstated, gathering eight points within the next three years can bring a second suspension.

cards.front: Which point totals trigger the clinic, a first suspension, and a suspension after reinstatement?
cards.back: Seven points can send you to a driver improvement clinic, while twelve points within three years can cost you the license; after reinstatement only eight points within three years can bring a second suspension.

decks.domain: Driving privilege: points, suspensions and restoration

cards.front: How long is a first, second and third point-system suspension?
cards.back: A point-system suspension lasts sixty days the first time, six months the second time and twelve months the third time.

cards.front: What is the adult point-system suspension ladder?
cards.back: The adult point-system ladder runs sixty days, then six months, then twelve months for the first, second and third suspension.

cards.front: What happens to your license points and insurance points when your privilege is reinstated?
cards.back: When your privilege is reinstated, every earlier driver license point is wiped out, but insurance points are not affected.

cards.front: How does the clinic's effect on points differ from reinstatement's effect?
cards.back: Completing the clinic removes three points, whereas reinstatement after a suspension cancels every earlier license point.

cards.front: Why do insurance points survive reinstatement?
cards.back: Reinstatement clears license points but leaves insurance points untouched, because insurers keep their own point system.

cards.front: Who sets the point system used for insurance rates?
cards.back: Insurance companies set rates with their own separate point system, and your insurance agent can answer questions about it.

decks.domain: Driving privilege: points, suspensions and restoration

cards.front: In a regular vehicle, which offenses carry the highest point value?
cards.back: In a regular vehicle, passing a stopped school bus and aggressive driving each carry five points, the highest values on the regular schedule.

cards.front: Which offenses such as reckless driving and tailgating carry four points?
cards.back: Illegal passing, reckless driving, tailgating (following too closely), a property-damage-only hit and run, and driving on the wrong side of the road each carry four points.

cards.front: How many points for failing to yield to a pedestrian, bicycle, scooter or motorcycle?
cards.back: Failing to yield to a pedestrian under the cited statute, or to a bicycle, motor scooter or motorcycle, carries four points.

cards.front: How many points for running a stop sign or red light, failing to yield, or speeding above fifty-five?
cards.back: Running a stop sign, running a red light, failing to yield right of way, and speeding faster than fifty-five miles per hour each carry three points.

cards.front: How many points for an expired license over a year, ignoring a siren, a safety zone, or no insurance?
cards.back: Driving with no license or one expired over a year, ignoring a siren, driving through a safety zone, and having no liability insurance each carry three points.

cards.front: How many points for skipping a required accident report or speeding in a posted school zone?
cards.back: Failing to file a required accident report and speeding above a posted school zone limit each carry three points.

cards.front: How many points for not restraining a child, and for any unlisted moving violation?
cards.back: Not properly restraining a child in a child restraint or seat belt carries two points, the same as any other moving violation not listed.

cards.front: How many points does littering with a motor vehicle carry?
cards.back: Littering that involves the use of a motor vehicle carries one point.

decks.domain: Driving privilege: points, suspensions and restoration

cards.front: In a commercial motor vehicle, how many points for passing a stopped school bus?
cards.back: While operating a commercial motor vehicle, passing a stopped school bus carries eight points.

cards.front: In a commercial motor vehicle, which offenses carry six points?
cards.back: In a commercial motor vehicle, a rail-highway crossing violation and aggressive driving each carry six points.

cards.front: In a commercial motor vehicle, how many points for reckless driving, a red light, and other moving violations?
cards.back: In a commercial motor vehicle, reckless driving carries five points, running a red light four points and any other moving violation three points.

cards.front: How many points for having alcohol in a commercial vehicle's passenger area?
cards.back: Having an alcoholic beverage in the passenger area of a commercial motor vehicle carries four points.

cards.front: How do the top commercial point values compare with the littering value?
cards.back: On the commercial schedule, passing a stopped school bus carries eight points and a rail-highway crossing violation six, yet littering with a vehicle still carries only one point.

cards.front: Which size and parking convictions add no points?
cards.back: Overload, overlength, overwidth and overheight convictions add no points, and neither does illegal parking.

cards.front: Which plate, equipment and weapon offenses add no points?
cards.back: Plate, registration, muffler, emblem and inspection-certificate offenses, and carrying a concealed weapon, add no points.

cards.front: How can fines change for a point offense committed in a commercial vehicle?
cards.back: A point-carrying offense committed in a commercial motor vehicle may be charged double any fine or penalty the statute authorizes.

decks.domain: Driving privilege: points, suspensions and restoration

cards.front: Besides court penalties, what can certain traffic convictions take away?
cards.back: On top of any criminal penalty from the court, conviction of certain traffic offenses takes away your driving privilege.

cards.front: Which speeding records over fifty-five within a year let DMV suspend your license?
cards.back: DMV can suspend your license for two over-fifty-five miles per hour speeding convictions within twelve months, or one over-fifty-five speeding conviction plus one reckless driving conviction within a year.

cards.front: Does willful racing have to be planned ahead to allow a suspension?
cards.back: A conviction for willful racing against another vehicle, planned ahead or not, lets DMV suspend your license.

cards.front: When else can DMV suspend for a court order or very high speed?
cards.back: DMV can also suspend when a court sentence orders you not to drive for a set time, and in certain cases after a conviction for speeding over seventy-five miles per hour

cards.front: What revocation follows driving more than fifteen over the limit while above fifty-five?
cards.back: Driving more than fifteen miles per hour over the limit while going faster than fifty-five miles per hour brings a revocation of at least thirty days.

cards.front: When does a high-speed revocation last sixty days instead?
cards.back: The revocation is sixty days for a second over-fifty-five, more-than-fifteen-over speeding charge within one year, or for speeding together with reckless driving on the same occasion.

cards.front: How do the thirty-day and sixty-day speeding revocations differ?
cards.back: Speeding more than fifteen miles per hour over the limit above fifty-five miles per hour means at least thirty days, but a second such charge within a year, or speeding plus reckless driving on one occasion, means sixty days.

decks.domain: Driving privilege: points, suspensions and restoration

cards.front: What suspension follows manslaughter, death by vehicle, or assault with a vehicle, and impaired manslaughter?
cards.back: Manslaughter, death by vehicle and assault with a motor vehicle each bring a one-year suspension, while manslaughter while impaired brings a permanent one.

cards.front: How does the suspension for manslaughter differ from manslaughter while impaired?
cards.back: Manslaughter brings a one-year suspension, while manslaughter under the influence of an impairing substance brings a permanent one.

cards.front: What suspension follows failing to stop and give aid, or refusing an alcohol test?
cards.back: Failing to stop and give aid after a crash, and willfully refusing a blood or breath alcohol test, each bring a one-year suspension.
cards.memory_hook: no aid or refusal, one year

cards.front: What suspension follows high-speed driving to avoid arrest?
cards.back: Speeding over fifty-five miles per hour and at least fifteen miles per hour over the limit while trying to avoid arrest brings a one-year suspension.

cards.front: What suspension follows two reckless driving charges in a year, or lying for a license?
cards.back: Two reckless driving charges within twelve months, or trying to get a license or learner permit under false pretenses, each bring a one-year suspension.
cards.memory_hook: repeat reckless or lies, one year

cards.front: What happens after a prearranged highway racing conviction, including to the car?
cards.back: Prearranged highway racing, and watching, betting on or lending a car for it, carry a three-year suspension, and the officer seizes the car, which a court may order sold at public auction after conviction.

cards.front: How does the racing suspension compare with most other offenses in the same table?
cards.back: Prearranged racing and helping with it carry three years, three times the one-year period for most other offenses in the same table.

cards.front: What penalty follows a failure to yield in the listed situations that causes serious bodily injury?
cards.back: Failing to yield in the listed situations, such as entering an intersection or at a highway construction or maintenance area, when the offense causes serious bodily injury brings ninety days and five hundred dollars.
cards.memory_hook: injury from not yielding, ninety days

decks.module: Hearings, other states and unpaid tickets
decks.domain: Driving privilege: points, suspensions and restoration

cards.front: When may DMV suspend after a conviction, and what may a revoked driver request?
cards.back: DMV may suspend your privilege as soon as it receives the conviction report from the court, and a revoked driver may have a right to a hearing in the judicial district where they live.

cards.front: If a DMV hearing does not help, where and how fast can you appeal?
cards.back: If the hearing does not help, you may appeal the DMV decision within thirty days to the Superior Court of your home county.

cards.front: Which comes first when challenging a revocation, the hearing or the court appeal?
cards.back: A revoked driver first asks DMV for a hearing; only if that fails is the appeal taken to the county Superior Court within thirty days.

cards.front: Can a conviction in another state affect your North Carolina license?
cards.back: A conviction in another state can lead to suspension or revocation of your North Carolina license as though it happened here, and DMV must notify you in writing of the effective date.

cards.front: What happens if you miss court or do not pay a fine for a citation?
cards.back: If you miss court or do not pay a fine for a citation, DMV sets a revocation date that takes effect unless the fine is paid or waived first, and it lasts until the court reports payment or waiver.

cards.front: Does paying a citation cancel the consequences of a conviction for the offense?
cards.back: Taking care of the citation does not cancel the consequences of the offense itself if you are convicted.

cards.front: What can you do if you cannot afford a traffic ticket?
cards.back: If you cannot afford a ticket, you file the Motion for Relief form with the clerk in the county where you got the ticket and ask for a hearing, where the judge may lower the amount, set a payment plan or waive it.

cards.front: If you can pay a ticket in full, how is the suspension stopped?
cards.back: If you can pay in full, you contact the clerk in that county, pay the whole amount, and the court tells DMV, which stops the suspension.

cards.front: How do the cannot-pay and can-pay routes differ, and what do they share?
cards.back: A driver who cannot pay files a Motion for Relief and asks the judge for relief, while a driver who can pay calls the clerk and pays everything; in both routes the court notifies DMV.
cards.memory_hook: relief or pay, court tells DMV

decks.domain: Driving privilege: points, suspensions and restoration

cards.front: What suspension does a provisional licensee under eighteen face for a second moving violation within a year?
cards.back: A provisional licensee under eighteen faces a thirty-day suspension for a second moving violation conviction within twelve months.

cards.front: What suspensions follow a provisional licensee's third and fourth moving violations within a year?
cards.back: A provisional licensee faces ninety days for a third and six months for a fourth moving violation conviction within twelve months.

cards.front: What is the provisional suspension ladder for repeat moving violations?
cards.back: For a provisional licensee the ladder runs thirty days, ninety days and six months, counted from the second, third and fourth moving violation within twelve months.

cards.front: What restoration fee clears an ordinary suspension, and when is it waived?
cards.back: Clearing a suspension or revocation requires a restoration fee of eighty-three point five zero dollars, except when the license was taken for medical reasons after a medical evaluation.

cards.front: What does restoring after a DWI revocation cost, and when is the service fee skipped?
cards.back: Restoring after a DWI revocation costs one hundred sixty-seven point two five dollars, and a fifty dollars service fee also applies unless you surrendered the license to the court or mailed it to DMV before the effective date.

cards.front: How do the ordinary and DWI restoration fees compare, and when is the service fee avoided?
cards.back: The ordinary restoration fee is eighty-three point five zero dollars and the DWI restoration fee is one hundred sixty-seven point two five dollars, while the separate fifty dollars service fee is skipped if the license was surrendered or mailed in before the effective date.

cards.front: What steps get your driving privilege back after a suspension?
cards.back: To get your privilege back you go to a driver license office, prove identity, pay the fees, reapply, take any required tests, show insurance if required and pay for the new license.

recap_hooks.text: Seven points can mean the clinic, which takes three off.
Twelve in three years suspends, and after reinstatement eight is enough.
Adult suspensions run sixty days, six months, then twelve months.
Reinstatement wipes license points, but insurance points stay.
Passing a stopped school bus and aggressive driving top the regular list at five.
Unlisted moving violations carry two points, and littering with a vehicle carries one.
In a commercial vehicle, passing a stopped school bus costs eight points.
Oversize, parking, plate and equipment offenses add no points.
Fifteen over while above fifty-five costs at least thirty days.
A second within a year, or speeding with reckless driving, costs sixty.
Most serious offenses cost one year, but impaired manslaughter is permanent.
Prearranged racing costs three years and the car.

recaps.module: Hearings, other states and unpaid tickets

recap_hooks.text: Ask for a hearing first, then appeal within thirty days.
Cannot pay a ticket? File for relief. Can pay? Pay the clerk in full.
Provisional drivers face thirty days, ninety days, then six months.
Restoring takes a fee, and a DWI restoration costs more.
